eval_rule: validation and (report-only) test every max(500, steps/40) steps; selection only by validation
title: DBP-X, Ns = 20: joint LS start of the cascade (direct_ld) at L = 63
question: Does the direct_ld arm of E054 (taps truncated to L, then joint fit of the cascade by Xiao's L_D with L-BFGS, then Adam on MSE) at L = 63 reach the progressive arm of E054 at L = 63 (99.07 %, 10 seeds)? Fills the missing point L = 63 of direct_ld in E054.
model: as E054: e054_prune.run(ns=20, mode='direct_ld', target=63) without changes; D_total exact and fixed; start = physical taps truncated to 63, L-BFGS 300 iterations on L_D (the lowest L_D kept), alpha and sign/multiplier of the E050 start choice (validation), complex gain by LS on train

schedule.iterations: e054_prune.iters_to(63) = warm 3000 + 2 x (shrink 1000 + fine 2000) = 9000 (the budget of the progressive arm up to L = 63)
schedule.optimizer: Adam 1e-3, 4 whole train files per iteration, circular shift, MSE on all symbols
schedule.selection: checkpoint with the minimum validation MSE (every 100 iterations); test reported there

rm: e054_prune.rm_both and dbpx.rm_columns at L = 63 (direct and FFT, 4 and 3 RM per complex product); the RM convention is not changed (pending advisor)

rule_draft.compare: direct_ld L63 (5 seeds) vs progressive L63 of E054 (10 seeds): a difference is a signal if |diff| > 2 SE and > 2 std (E054 rule); otherwise 'no difference proven'
rule_draft.report: mean, std, SE, range over seeds; share of the progressive L = 255 level kept; RM in both conventions; L_D before/after L-BFGS
rule_draft.limits: one schedule, no tuning; 5 seeds; circular files; one channel, one polarization, 1 sps; the reference arm is from another experiment (same code, same data, same start choice)

value_filter.changes_next_step: yes: whether the joint LS start keeps its advantage when the filter is long enough (L = 63) or the two starts coincide
